subject: Vendor onboarding: invoice delivery playbook and exception paths
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <accounts-payable@zencomponents.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on invoice submission (portal vs email)

Hi Hannah / Laura,

We're in the final stage of setting Zen Components up in your vendor registry. Before we submit our first weekly invoice I'd like to confirm the preferred delivery method and required fields so our billing system maps correctly. A few quick questions: 

- Do you prefer invoices via the Redwood Vendor Portal or to ap-invoices@redwood.com?
- If email is accepted, what exact subject line and filename convention should we use to avoid manual routing?
- Which PO number field should we populate (PO in header, line-level PO, or both)?
- Are there mandatory columns you require on the invoice line items (e.g., item code, cost center, GL code)?

I've attached our current invoice template (vendor_invoice_template.xlsx) and a filled sample for the trial week. Also attaching our W9.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick screen-share if that helps.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Accounts Payable | Zen Components
attachments: vendor_invoice_template.xlsx, sample-week1-invoice.xlsx, W9_ZenComponents.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on invoice submission (portal vs email)

Hi Lena — welcome, and thanks for the files. High level guidance below; Marcus (Finance) is copied for the rules and exception paths.

Preferred method: Vendor Portal (https://portal.redwood.com/vendor-signup) — it gives faster PO matching and eliminates manual emails. Please sign up and request onboarding access; procurement will approve and you get a vendor ID.

If portal onboarding will take longer than 48 hours, interim option: email invoices to ap-invoices@redwood.com with subject: REDWOOD_INV | PO{PO_NUMBER} | ZenComponents | YYYYMMDD. Example: REDWOOD_INV | PO123456 | ZenComponents | 20261129.xlsx. 

Required fields for both portal and email uploads:
- PO number (exact text: PO:) in invoice header
- Invoice number
- Invoice date
- Line-level description, quantity, unit price, line total
- Cost center or GL code (if not provided, charge will be held and we will request a resubmit)

I attached our standard invoice template (Redwood_invoice_template_v2.xlsx) — please try to populate matching column names to avoid mapping issues.

We will set up a 30-minute onboarding call on Monday to walk through the portal and mapping. If there are any exceptions (no PO or MSA-driven credits), Marcus will outline the approval steps.

Laura Bennett
Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_invoice_template_v2.xlsx

Lena

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <accounts-payable@zencomponents.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on invoice submission (portal vs email) — finance rules and exception flows

Hi Lena — brief finance-side rules to make sure your AR team routes correctly: 

1) PO presence: For automated 3-way match we require the PO number both in the invoice header and in the filename or email subject for interim email uploads. If one is missing we'll queue the invoice for manual review which delays payment.

2) No-PO exceptions: If a PO is issued retroactively (e.g., for onboarding month), please submit the invoice to ap-invoices@redwood.com and include a cover email with the related SOW or MSA reference. Mark the subject with EXCEPTION and the estimated PO number when available. Finance will create a hold code (HOLD-PO-PEND) and will escalate for approval; expected resolution time is 5 business days if supporting docs are provided.

3) Credit memos: yes — submit through the portal where possible. If you must email, subject should start with REDWOOD_CREDIT | ZenComponents | MEMO123. Credits without matching invoice references will be held.

4) File formats: Portal accepts PDF & XLSX. Email ingest prefers PDF; if you send XLSX, please also attach a PDF copy.

5) Turnaround: Standard terms are Net 45 from invoice receipt post successful match. For vendor portal-uploaded invoices we prioritize processing within 10 business days. For exception/emailed invoices timeline can stretch to Net 60 due to manual review.

6) Contact & escalation: ap-invoices@redwood.com is monitored. For escalations contact me directly (marcus_lin@redwood.com).

We'll work with Procurement to provision your portal account today. Expect invite from vendor-portal@redwood.com.

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference

Hi Lena — quick summary and next steps from Procurement/Finance: 

1) Primary path: Sign up for the Vendor Portal and upload invoices there. Portal uploads get fastest processing (target 10 business days). Link: https://portal.redwood.com/vendor-signup
2) Interim path: Email ap-invoices@redwood.com with subject format: REDWOOD_INV | PO{PO_NUMBER} | ZenComponents | YYYYMMDD (include PDF copy). If no PO yet, mark subject with EXCEPTION and attach SOW/MSA.
3) Mandatory fields: PO in header, invoice number, invoice date, line-level description, qty, unit price, line total, cost center/GL. Use the attached Redwood_invoice_template_v2.xlsx as the mapping reference.
4) Credits: use REDWOOD_CREDIT subject or the portal credit upload.
5) Timeline: Portal = prioritized (10 business days). Email/exception = manual review (may be Net 60).

Action items: 
- Lena: confirm you received the vendor portal invite and whether you can switch to the Redwood template by EOD Monday (2026-11-29).
- Laura: confirm portal provisioning for Zen Components and send invite (Procurement).
- Marcus: track initial invoices under HOLD-PO-PEND if PO is retroactive and aim for 5 business day resolution.

If all good I'll schedule the 30-minute onboarding call Monday afternoon and include a short screen-share on the portal upload and mapping. Thanks everyone.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
